newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares continue fall, no end in sight.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares continue fall, no end in sight.

text.p: Singapore shares continued falling on Friday and dealers said they saw no immediate end in sight to the weakness and pessimism.
"The Singapore market is not likely to bounce back in the near future and will continue low well into next week," said one dealer glumly.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index had fallen 20.13 or 0.98 percent to 2,075.30 by 0245 GMT.
Dealers said the fall was a spillover from Thursday's shock of non-oil domestic exports falling 7.9 percent year on year in February and continued disappointment with corporate results.
Keppel Corp shares were an early casualty, plunging to a three-year low of Singapore $9.30 in the first 30 minutes and continuing their slide to S$9.20 by 0245 GMT.
Early market volume was a mild 43.3 million units with losers led by Great Eastern Life, down S$0.40 at S$22.00 after announcing a 21.3 percent profit fall late on Thursday.
Over-the-counter-traded Kuala Lumpur Industries shares led the early gainers, rising S$0.40 to S$2.82.
Kian Ho Bearings topped the actives at 0245 GMT, down S$0.02 at S$0.67 on volume of 1.6 million units.
